On November 12, 2026, CorMedix Inc. (the “Company” or “CorMedix”) hosted a conference call and webcast for investors to discuss its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. A copy of the transcript of the conference call is furnished with this Current Report on Form 8-K as Exhibit 99.1 and is incorporated by reference herein. The information in this Item 7.01 (including Exhibit 99.1) shall not be deemed “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), or otherwise subject to the liabilities of that section, nor shall it be deemed incorporated by reference in any filing under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), or the Exchange Act, except as expressly set forth by specific reference in such a filing. Additional Information and Where to Find It In connection with the Proposed Acquisition (as defined below), Heron Therapeutics, Inc. (“Heron”) intends to file with the SEC a proxy statement on Schedule 14A. Each of CorMedix and Heron has and may file relevant documents with the SEC regarding the Proposed Acquisition. This Current Report on Form 8-K is not a substitute for the proxy statement or any other document that CorMedix or Heron may file with the SEC. Heron will mail the definitive proxy statement to its stockholders. INVESTORS AND STOCKHOLDERS ARE URGED TO READ THE PROXY STATEMENT AND ANY OTHER RELEVANT DOCUMENTS FILED WITH THE SEC , AS WELL AS ANY AMENDMENTS OR SUPPLEMENTS TO THOSE DOCUMENTS, CAREFULLY AND IN THEIR ENTIRETY WHEN THEY BECOME AVAILABLE, BECAUSE THEY WILL CONTAIN IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT THE PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Investors and stockholders may obtain these documents free of charge at the SEC’s website, www.sec.gov, and on the Investors section of CorMedix’s investor relations website at https://cormedix.com/investors/ and Heron’s investor relations website at https://ir.herontx.com/. Participants in the Solicitation CorMedix, Heron and their respective directors and executive officers may be deemed to be participants in the solicitation of proxies from Heron’s stockholders in connection with the Proposed Acquisition. Information about the directors and executive officers of Heron, including a description of their direct or indirect interests, by security holdings or otherwise, is set forth in its proxy statement for its 2026 annual meeting of stockholders, filed with the SEC on April 30, 2026, which is available online at https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/818033/000119312526196306/hrtx-20260430.htm, under the headings “Information Concerning the Board of Directors,” “Information Concerning Executive Officers,” “Corporate Governance – 2025 Director Compensation,” “Security Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management,” “Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions” and “Executive Compensation,” and information about the directors and executive officers of CorMedix, including a description of their direct or indirect interests, by security holdings or otherwise, is set forth in its proxy statement for its 2026 annual meeting of stockholders, filed with the SEC on April 29, 2026, which is available online at https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/1410098/000121390026049311/ea0286136-05.htm, under the headings “Proposal No. 1 – Approval of the Director Election Proposal,” “Corporate Governance – Executive Officers,” “Security Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management,” “Director Compensation,” “Executive Compensation” and “Certain Relationships and Related Transactions,” and, in each case, in subsequently filed Current Reports on Form 8-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q and Forms 3, 4 and 5. Additional information regarding the interests of such participants will be included in the proxy statement and other relevant materials to be filed with the SEC when they become available. Other information regarding the participants in the solicitation and a description of their direct and indirect interests, by security holdings or otherwise, will be set forth in Heron’s definitive proxy statement and other relevant materials to be filed with the SEC regarding the Proposed Acquisition when such materials become available. Investors and stockholders should read the proxy statement carefully when it becomes available before making any voting or investment decisions. Copies of these documents may be obtained, free of charge, from the sources indicated above. No Offer or Solicitation This Current Report on Form 8-K is for informational purposes only and does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy any securities, or a solicitation of any vote or approval, nor shall there be any sale of securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such jurisdiction. The shares of CorMedix common stock to be issued to Heron in the Proposed Acquisition will be issued in a private placement in reliance on an exemption from the registration requirements of the Securities Act and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from registration. 1 Forward-Looking Statements This Current Report on Form 8-K contains “forward-looking statements” within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, Section 27A of the Securities Act and Section 21E of the Exchange Act, that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Forward-looking statements are often identified by the use of words such as, but not limited to, “anticipate,” “believe,” “can,” “continue,” “could,” “estimate,” “expect,” “guidance,” “intend,” “may,” “plan,” “potential,” “project,” “seek,” “should,” “target,” “will,” “would,” and similar expressions. All statements, other than statements of historical facts, regarding management’s expectations, beliefs, goals, plans or CorMedix’s prospects should be considered forward-looking statements, including, but not limited to, statements regarding financial and business guidance; sales, revenue and operating expense estimates; Adjusted EBITDA estimates; expectations regarding product utilization and sales; the 2027 post-TDAPA Add-on for DefenCath, including the quarterly methodology adopted by CMS, CorMedix’s ability to reach pricing arrangements with dialysis customers that track quarterly Add-on adjustments, and CorMedix’s dependence on a limited number of large dialysis organization customers; CorMedix’s ability to secure separate payment for DefenCath from Medicare Advantage plans; the timing and outcome of FDA review of the REZZAYO sNDA; expectations and timing regarding clinical trials and development, performance expectations and revenue opportunities of CorMedix’s product pipeline; expectations regarding implementation and perceived benefits of CorMedix’s products; the proposed acquisition by CorMedix of substantially all of the assets of Heron (the “Proposed Acquisition”); Heron’s ability to provide an additional revenue base of four FDA-approved commercial brands, with opportunities to drive future growth; the expected timing of closing; the anticipated benefits of the Proposed Acquisition, including expected synergies, diversification of revenue base and the expectation that the Proposed Acquisition will be accretive to earnings; statements regarding product strategy, growth and label expansion opportunities; development and expectations of CorMedix’s and Heron’s product pipeline, results of real-world studies, expectations regarding product utilization, reimbursement rates, and market access, including changes in CMS reimbursement methodology; the potential achievement of earn-out milestones and royalty payments; the commercial potential of ZYNRELEF and the other acquired products; the development of the acquired pipeline program; the terms, funding and availability of the Pharmakon term loan facility; CorMedix’s ability to pursue future business development transactions; and estimates of total addressable market size. These statements are based on current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially, including: the failure to obtain Heron stockholder approval or required regulatory clearances, or to satisfy other closing conditions, on a timely basis or at all; CorMedix’s ability to successfully integrate the acquired assets, achieve anticipated synergies, accretion, and EBITDA or Adjusted EBITDA on a timely basis or at all; the amount of any adjustments to the consideration under the asset purchase agreement; the occurrence of any event that could give rise to termination of the asset purchase agreement, including circumstances requiring Heron to pay a termination fee; the risk that CorMedix’s or Heron’s stock price may decline if the Proposed Acquisition is not completed; fluctuations in the price of CorMedix common stock; dilution to CorMedix’s stockholders; disruption to CorMedix’s and Heron’s business relationships with customers, suppliers and employees, including as a result of the announcement or pendency of the Proposed Acquisition, and diversion of management’s attention; restrictions on the conduct of Heron’s business while the Proposed Acquisition is pending; unexpected costs, liabilities or delays relating to the Proposed Acquisition and the acquired products; market acceptance and reimbursement of the acquired products, including continued eligibility for separate payment under the NOPAIN Act; changes to reimbursement rates and methodology, customer utilization, and other factors impacting the demand for CorMedix’s and Heron’s products; continued pricing pressures and the impact of actions of governmental and private payers affecting pricing of, reimbursement for, and patient access to pharmaceuticals and reporting obligations related thereto; competition; the expiration of intellectual property protection for certain of the company’s products and competition from generic and biosimilar products; the risk that topline data from CorMedix’s and its partners’ clinical trials, including the ReSPECT study, that CorMedix announces or publishes from time to time may change as more patient data become available or may be interpreted differently if additional data is disclosed; failure to successfully conduct future clinical trials, including due to CorMedix’s or its partners’ potential inability to enroll or retain sufficient patients to conduct and complete the trials, including the Phase 3 TPN study for DefenCath, or generate data necessary for regulatory approval, among other things; development of unexpected safety or efficacy concerns related to CorMedix’s product candidates; manufacturing and supply risks; the incurrence of indebtedness and compliance with covenants under the Pharmakon facility; litigation relating to the Proposed Acquisition; uncertainty about CorMedix’s or Heron’s business, operations and strategy after the consummation of the Proposed Acquisition; and the other risks described in the periodic reports filed by CorMedix and Heron with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”), including their most recent Annual Reports on Form 10-K and Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, including CorMedix’s Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, copies of which are available free of charge at the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov or upon request from CorMedix and Heron, as applicable. In addition, pro forma financial information does not necessarily reflect the actual results that we would have achieved had the pro forma transaction been consummated as of the date indicated nor does it reflect the potential future results of the combined company. All forward-looking statements are expressly qualified in their entirety by this cautionary statement, and readers are cautioned not to place undue reliance on them. Forward-looking statements speak only as of the date of this Current Report on Form 8-K, and neither CorMedix nor Heron undertakes any obligation to update them, except as required by law.
